name: Salesforce Tower
from: As #423 (engine/bay/heroes.json on PR 428): Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation) for its outline and height; its taper off a photograph. Its far model is the Ina wedge's (landing/ina/heroes.mjs).

name: Golden Gate Bridge
from: As #423 (PR 428): Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation) for its place, turn and towers; the bridge district's published figures for spans, heights, cables and truss.

name: Transamerica Pyramid
from: Its point, 263.5 m over the sea at this place: the release's own far tiles (USGS 3DEP lidar), which are what is drawn of it. Its 260 m as published, so its foot is 3.5 m. Only its light by night is by rule here (heroes.rs `night`: the spire and its beacon); its shape is the map's building.

name: Bay Bridge, western span
from: As #423 (PR 428). Its far model is the Ina wedge's.

name: Ferry Building
from: Outline 202 by 56 m along bearing 143 degrees, 15 to 16 m high, and the clock tower's seven stages over a 12 m square to 70 m: Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation). Its foot: USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation, 3.46 m NAVD88. Arcade, clock and belfry by eye. The rule is engine/core/src/heroes.rs.

name: Sutro Tower
from: Height 298 m and its platforms' triangles at 55, 115, 168, 198 and 230 m: Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation). Its foot: USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation, 255.3 m NAVD88. Bracing and bands by eye. The rule is engine/core/src/heroes.rs.

name: City Hall
from: Outline 127 by 98 m, 30 m high, the cross wing and the rotunda's stages to the dome at 75 m: Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation); the dome's top at 93.6 m (307.5 feet) as published. Its foot: USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation, 18.55 m NAVD88. Colonnades, courts and gilding by eye. The rule is engine/core/src/heroes.rs.

name: Palace of Fine Arts
from: The rotunda's place and its height of 49 m (162 feet) as published; the exhibition hall behind is the map's (Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0, © OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation). Its foot: USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation, 2.68 m NAVD88. Piers, arches, colonnade, planter boxes and swan lagoon by rule in engine/core/src/heroes.rs.

name: Fort Point
from: Third System brick coastal fort (1861) directly beneath the Golden Gate Bridge's south arch: footprint and elevation from DataSF/Overture Maps (© OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation) and USGS 3DEP. Rule in engine/core/src/heroes.rs.

name: California Academy of Sciences
from: The DataSF footprint separates the 161 by 102 m canopy from a 5.5 m-wide path. The roof heights come from the 0.25 m lidar in square 546.7_4179.5. NAIP locates the piazza glazing and the two unequal skylight fields. Individual openings and window mullions are illustrative. Roof reference: https://www.fondazionerenzopiano.org/en/project/california-academy-of-sciences/image-717.pdf

name: Japanese Tea Garden
from: Golden Gate Park Japanese Tea Garden (1894). Fence, pond, Pagoda, Tea House, Main Gate, Drum Bridge, footbridge and Peace Lantern placed from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL; ways 30900516, 409163924, 34221099, 34220947, 494967002, 136898969, 34218824; read 2026-11-26); the Gift Shop and Temple Gate are left to the map. Zen garden, trees and other lanterns are unchecked. Rule in engine/core/src/heroes.rs.

name: San Francisco Botanical Garden
from: San Francisco Botanical Garden, Golden Gate Park, round its Great Meadow and main gate. Fountain court and flowerbeds placed from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL; ways 476290501, 1036243321, 1064976638, 1072073350, 1063385914, 1072073345; read 2026-11-26). OSM maps no pond, pavilion or glasshouse in this box, so none is drawn; the County Fair Building, toilets, bookstore and ticket kiosk are left to the map. Trees and the meadow walk are unchecked. Rule in engine/core/src/heroes.rs.

name: Conservatory of Flowers
from: Victorian white-framed glazed glasshouse (1879) and Conservatory Valley geometric floral carpet parterres. Outline and terrace elevation from DataSF/Overture Maps and USGS 3DEP. Rule in engine/core/src/heroes.rs.

name: Painted Ladies
from: 710-722 Steiner Street (1892-1896): seven stepped Queen Anne Victorian rowhouses facing Alamo Square. Lot positions and hillside elevations surveyed from DataSF footprints and USGS 3DEP; colours from Alamo Square reference photography. Rule in engine/core/src/heroes.rs.

name: de Young Museum
from: Herzog & de Meuron (2005): 150 by 74 m oxidized copper-clad museum with cantilevered Music Concourse overhang and 44 m twisting Hamon Observation Tower. Footprint and tower position from DataSF/Overture Maps and USGS 3DEP. Rule in engine/core/src/heroes.rs.
